newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks still winning buyers.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks still winning buyers.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks powered ahead Wednesday as the Dow Jones industrial average continued its spectacular rise with the help of powerhouse International Business Machines Corp.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow was up 21.99 points at 6,419.59, beating Tuesday's record close of 6,397.60, which was its 40th record close this year.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on active volume of 270 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 3.71 points at 1,266.33, and the American Stock Exchange index rose 1.63 to 586.27.
Analysts had different views on where the market would go from here, but almost all were surprised by the explosive runup in the Dow index.
Talk of a near-term correction, which had been widespread in the past few days, was nearly silenced.

"It's really been amazing. Also frightening, scary, wonderful and energetic. This market wants to go up and you don't want to stand in its way," said John Gardner, chief equity strategist at Van Lieu Capital.
The Dow's gains soundly beat the broader market, which has caused some concern among analysts.
IBM continued its stunning ascent, climbing 2-1/4 to 156 and hitting highs it has not seen since 1987.
Traders said the company was being viewed as a safe haven among technology shares, especially due to its low valuation vs. other high tech stocks.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 8/32, sending its yield up to 6.45 percent from 6.44 percent at Tuesday's close as traders awaited Wednesday's government auction of $12.5 billion of five year notes.
Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter, said the low yield on bonds was helping to drive the stock market.
"The reason is simple -- interest rates have continued to fall. The stock market has moved perfectly in sync with bonds and is now appropriately seeking higher levels," he said.

Canelo said he did not fear a major correction soon because "the scary blow-offs we've had in the past in the market have been characterised by rising bond yields and strong economies," neither of which is currently in place.
Many analysts who earlier this week expected an imminent technical correction were defied by the Dow's performance.
Still, some strategists sought to protect themselves from a possible fall.
One brokerage house, Prime Charter Ltd., said Wednesday that it raised cash by 20 percent and reduced stock and bond holdings by 10 percent each in its model portfolio.

"We feel activity in the first-tier, largest capitalised names have reached frenetic levels, and the narrowness of their advance is cause for some concern," said Prime's chief market strategist, Scott Bleier. He also said further bond market gains would be minimal.
The winners among the blue-chip stocks included Caterpillar Inc., which jumped 3-7/8 to 77-3/4 after Smith Barney raised its opinion of the machinery giant.
Boeing's stock gained 2-1/8 at 96-1/8 on media reports that AMR Corp., the parent of American Airlines, would announce Thursday an order for up to $6 billion in Boeing planes. AMR was off 5/8 at 91.
